00:17:33.510 --> 00:17:36.720
but in West Jakarta, it's around 64 to 67 years,

469
00:17:36.720 --> 00:17:38.640
which is a clear 10-year gap.

470
00:17:38.640 --> 00:17:40.920
Same hospitals, you might have said:

471
00:17:40.920 --> 00:17:42.420
Wealthy residents have better access

472
00:17:42.420 --> 00:17:45.030
to high-quality healthcare, often private,

473
00:17:45.030 --> 00:17:48.450
while low-income areas often lack reliable medical services.

474
00:17:48.450 --> 00:17:51.450
For kampungs have more green space, you might have said:

475
00:17:51.450 --> 00:17:54.030
Kampungs are more crowded and have limited green space.

476
00:17:54.030 --> 00:17:58.410
Jakarta lost 33% of its green space between 2000 and 2020,

477
00:17:58.410 --> 00:18:00.720
affecting poor districts most.

478
00:18:00.720 --> 00:18:03.510
Poor areas get more help, you might have said:

479
00:18:03.510 --> 00:18:05.550
Government and private investment is concentrated

480
00:18:05.550 --> 00:18:07.980
in wealthy areas, which have better infrastructure,

481
00:18:07.980 --> 00:18:10.230
schools, sanitation and services.

482
00:18:10.230 --> 00:18:11.130
Well done on this task.

483
00:18:11.130 --> 00:18:12.240
I hope you managed to include some

484
00:18:12.240 --> 00:18:14.130
of those points in your answers.

485
00:18:14.130 --> 00:18:15.690
We're now going to explore our final question

486
00:18:15.690 --> 00:18:16.830
of today's lesson.

487
00:18:16.830 --> 00:18:19.740
What are the challenges of managing inequality?

488
00:18:19.740 --> 00:18:21.600
Jakarta is a city of contrasts,

489
00:18:21.600 --> 00:18:23.040
and inequality here is the result

490
00:18:23.040 --> 00:18:24.900
of deep-rooted social and economic divides

491
00:18:24.900 --> 00:18:26.340
that have grown over time.

492
00:18:26.340 --> 00:18:28.080
Take South Jakarta for example.

493
00:18:28.080 --> 00:18:30.090
It's known for its green space, modern housing,

494
00:18:30.090 --> 00:18:32.310
private schools, and mostly formal employment

495
00:18:32.310 --> 00:18:34.170
with stable jobs and regular pay.

496
00:18:34.170 --> 00:18:35.640
Now, compare that to North Jakarta,

497
00:18:35.640 --> 00:18:38.610
where you'll find densely packed kampungs, poor sanitation,

498
00:18:38.610 --> 00:18:40.440
pollution, and mostly informal work,

499
00:18:40.440 --> 00:18:42.600
which is often low-paid and insecure.

500
00:18:42.600 --> 00:18:44.460
This contrast isn't accidental.

501
00:18:44.460 --> 00:18:46.410
Development has favored wealthier areas,

502
00:18:46.410 --> 00:18:47.610
where investment is profitable

503
00:18:47.610 --> 00:18:49.260
and services are well planned.

504
00:18:49.260 --> 00:18:51.840
Meanwhile, poorer communities, especially kampungs,

505
00:18:51.840 --> 00:18:53.130
often get left behind

506
00:18:53.130 --> 00:18:55.200
without the infrastructure or support they need.

507
00:18:55.200 --> 00:18:58.320
By 2025, Jakarta's 11.6 million residents

508
00:18:58.320 --> 00:19:00.750
are facing a city that's increasingly unequal,

509
00:19:00.750 --> 00:19:03.330
unless action is taken to ensure development is fair,

510
00:19:03.330 --> 00:19:06.150
inclusive, and focused on those who need it most.

511
00:19:06.150 --> 00:19:08.130
Which of the following best describes the difference

512
00:19:08.130 --> 00:19:10.170
between South and North Jakarta?

513
00:19:10.170 --> 00:19:12.180
A, North Jakarta has more private schools

514
00:19:12.180 --> 00:19:14.160
and green space than South Jakarta;

515
00:19:14.160 --> 00:19:15.867
B, South Jakarta is known for its kampungs

516
00:19:15.867 --> 00:19:17.640
and informal employment;

517
00:19:17.640 --> 00:19:20.100
C, North Jakarta experiences poor sanitation

518
00:19:20.100 --> 00:19:21.570
and higher pollution levels;

519
00:19:21.570 --> 00:19:23.520
D, South Jakarta struggles with overcrowding

520
00:19:23.520 --> 00:19:24.990
and lack of modern housing.

521
00:19:24.990 --> 00:19:26.520
Pause the video here whilst you decide,

522
00:19:26.520 --> 00:19:28.703
and press play when you're ready to continue.

523
00:19:32.910 --> 00:19:33.750
Excellent.

524
00:19:33.750 --> 00:19:35.010
The answers are C,

525
00:19:35.010 --> 00:19:37.140
North Jakarta experiences poor sanitation

526
00:19:37.140 --> 00:19:38.520
and higher pollution levels.

527
00:19:38.520 --> 00:19:39.630
Well done.

528
00:19:39.630 --> 00:19:41.910
Inequality in Jakarta isn't just about money.

529
00:19:41.910 --> 00:19:43.620
It's about how the city manages growth,

530
00:19:43.620 --> 00:19:45.330
development and fairness.

531
00:19:45.330 --> 00:19:48.060
First, rapid development growth puts major pressure

532
00:19:48.060 --> 00:19:50.190
on water, power and transport systems.

533
00:19:50.190 --> 00:19:53.310
As more people move in, infrastructure can't always keep up.

534
00:19:53.310 --> 00:19:55.800
Second, flooding and land sinking are getting worse

535
00:19:55.800 --> 00:19:58.590
due to overdevelopment, especially on vulnerable land.

536
00:19:58.590 --> 00:20:02.130
These floods now cost the city around $520 million per year

537
00:20:02.130 --> 00:20:03.900
in damage and disruption.

538
00:20:03.900 --> 00:20:05.370
Third, when the government tries

539
00:20:05.370 --> 00:20:08.670
to relocate kampung residents, it often sparks protests.

540
00:20:08.670 --> 00:20:12.330
In fact, 60% of kampung residents reject relocation.

541
00:20:12.330 --> 00:20:13.500
They fear losing community,

542
00:20:13.500 --> 00:20:15.720
jobs and security in the process.

543
00:20:15.720 --> 00:20:18.960
This reminds us that solving inequality isn't simple.

544
00:20:18.960 --> 00:20:21.090
It's about balancing the needs of different groups,

545
00:20:21.090 --> 00:20:23.100
avoiding harm, and making sure change is fair,

546
00:20:23.100 --> 00:20:25.050
inclusive and sustainable.

547
00:20:25.050 --> 00:20:26.550
Which of the following is a consequence

548
00:20:26.550 --> 00:20:28.470
of social inequality of Jakarta?

549
00:20:28.470 --> 00:20:31.590
Is it A, protests over kampung evictions;

550
00:20:31.590 --> 00:20:34.380
B, land subsidence due to overdevelopment;

551
00:20:34.380 --> 00:20:36.900
C, lack of citywide recycling schemes;

552
00:20:36.900 --> 00:20:39.240
or D, seasonal flooding from heavy rainfall?

553
00:20:39.240 --> 00:20:40.650
Pause the video here whilst you decide,

554
00:20:40.650 --> 00:20:42.893
and press play when you're ready to continue.

555
00:20:46.590 --> 00:20:47.423
Excellent.

556
00:20:47.423 --> 00:20:51.360
The answer is A, protests over kampung evictions. Well done.

557
00:20:51.360 --> 00:20:54.270
Jakarta faces huge challenges from poverty to flooding,

558
00:20:54.270 --> 00:20:55.170
but at the same time,

559
00:20:55.170 --> 00:20:56.850
the government is spending billions of dollars

560
00:20:56.850 --> 00:21:00.000
to build a brand new capital city called Nusantara.

561
00:21:00.000 --> 00:21:01.140
Let's compare.

562
00:21:01.140 --> 00:21:05.580
Jakarta urgently needs $4.2 billion just for flood defenses,

563
00:21:05.580 --> 00:21:07.620
1.2 million affordable homes,

564
00:21:07.620 --> 00:21:10.650
a fix for 35% water loss from leaking pipes,

565
00:21:10.650 --> 00:21:14.880
a $6.5 billion infrastructure upgrade, and better education

566
00:21:14.880 --> 00:21:17.970
only 60% of kampung residents currently have.

567
00:21:17.970 --> 00:21:21.720
Meanwhile, Nusantara is costing 30 billion overall,

568
00:21:21.720 --> 00:21:25.260
with plans to move 16,000 civil servants in 2024.

569
00:21:25.260 --> 00:21:27.780
It's designed to be 65% green space,

570
00:21:27.780 --> 00:21:29.820
powered by 75% renewables,

571
00:21:29.820 --> 00:21:33.270
and include $1.5 billion in smart technology.

572
00:21:33.270 --> 00:21:34.650
So here's the key question.

573
00:21:34.650 --> 00:21:37.170
Can Indonesia truly tackle inequality in Jakarta

574
00:21:37.170 --> 00:21:40.200
while putting so much funding and focus into Nusantara?

575
00:21:40.200 --> 00:21:41.910
It's a debate about priorities.

576
00:21:41.910 --> 00:21:43.560
Should more be done to improve conditions

577
00:21:43.560 --> 00:21:44.820
where people already live,

578
00:21:44.820 --> 00:21:48.060
or is investing in a future city the best long-term plan?

579
00:21:48.060 --> 00:21:49.590
The government has launched a range of reforms

580
00:21:49.590 --> 00:21:51.750
to improve Jakarta and reduce inequality,

581
00:21:51.750 --> 00:21:54.120
but not all of them are progressing smoothly.

582
00:21:54.120 --> 00:21:55.710
This chart shows a mix of actions

583
00:21:55.710 --> 00:21:59.250
that are ongoing, stalled, or still just promised.

584
00:21:59.250 --> 00:22:02.160
For example, flood defenses are making progress,

585
00:22:02.160 --> 00:22:04.980
but they are one of the few projects marked as ongoing.

586
00:22:04.980 --> 00:22:06.600
But kampung upgrades, transport links

587
00:22:06.600 --> 00:22:08.550
and affordable housings have stalled.

588
00:22:08.550 --> 00:22:10.770
Other pledges like government decentralization

589
00:22:10.770 --> 00:22:12.270
haven't started at all.

590
00:22:12.270 --> 00:22:14.850
Meanwhile, massive resources are going to Nusantara,

591
00:22:14.850 --> 00:22:17.700
the new capital, shown here in orange as promised,

592
00:22:17.700 --> 00:22:19.980
but already taking attention and funding.

593
00:22:19.980 --> 00:22:21.270
So what's going wrong?

594
00:22:21.270 --> 00:22:24.570
Some key challenges are corruption slowing down progress,

595
00:22:24.570 --> 00:22:26.310
budget problems delaying upgrades,

596
00:22:26.310 --> 00:22:28.200
and a major focus on Nusantara,

597
00:22:28.200 --> 00:22:29.430
which is pulling resources away

598
00:22:29.430 --> 00:22:31.800
from where they are urgently needed in Jakarta.

599
00:22:31.800 --> 00:22:34.170
So yes, reforms are underway,

600
00:22:34.170 --> 00:22:37.260
but their actual impact on inequality remains uncertain.

601
00:22:37.260 --> 00:22:40.470
Without consistent funding, transparency and follow through,

602
00:22:40.470 --> 00:22:43.950
real change may still be out of reach for many residents.

603
00:22:43.950 --> 00:22:44.790
True or false?

604
00:22:44.790 --> 00:22:47.040
The government is spending more on building Nusantara

605
00:22:47.040 --> 00:22:48.900
than on solving Jakarta's inequality issues

606
00:22:48.900 --> 00:22:51.210
like housing, flooding and education.

607
00:22:51.210 --> 00:22:52.530
Pause the video here whilst you decide,

608
00:22:52.530 --> 00:22:54.683
and press play when you're ready to continue.

609
00:22:59.550 --> 00:23:01.800
Excellent. This statement is true.

610
00:23:01.800 --> 00:23:03.330
I would like you to explain why.

611
00:23:03.330 --> 00:23:04.163
Pause the video here,

612
00:23:04.163 --> 00:23:06.263
and press play when you're ready to continue.

613
00:23:10.530 --> 00:23:11.363
Fantastic.

614
00:23:11.363 --> 00:23:13.800
The reason why it's true is because the total cost

615
00:23:13.800 --> 00:23:16.100
of Nusantara is estimated at 30 billion.

616
00:23:16.100 --> 00:23:16.933
At the same time,

617
00:23:16.933 --> 00:23:19.560
Jakarta needs 4.2 billion for flood defenses,

618
00:23:19.560 --> 00:23:21.600
6.5 billion for infrastructure,

619
00:23:21.600 --> 00:23:23.790
and 1.2 million affordable homes,

620
00:23:23.790 --> 00:23:25.860
but much of this remains underfunded.

621
00:23:25.860 --> 00:23:27.240
This highlights a funding imbalance

622
00:23:27.240 --> 00:23:29.580
when trying to tackle inequality in Jakarta.

623
00:23:29.580 --> 00:23:32.310
Well done if you managed to explain that correctly.

624
00:23:32.310 --> 00:23:34.290
Why is the impact of Jakarta's government reforms

625
00:23:34.290 --> 00:23:36.180
on inequality still uncertain?

626
00:23:36.180 --> 00:23:39.540
Is it A, all reforms have been successfully completed;

627
00:23:39.540 --> 00:23:42.900
B, progress has slowed as a result of Nusantara;

628
00:23:42.900 --> 00:23:45.510
C, Jakarta no longer has inequality issues;

629
00:23:45.510 --> 00:23:48.660
or D, all government spending is on kampung upgrades?

630
00:23:48.660 --> 00:23:50.100
Pause the video here whilst you decide,

631
00:23:50.100 --> 00:23:52.343
and press play when you're ready to continue.

632
00:23:57.600 --> 00:23:58.530
Fantastic.

633
00:23:58.530 --> 00:24:00.330
The answer is B, progress has slowed

634
00:24:00.330 --> 00:24:01.740
as a result of Nusantara.

635
00:24:01.740 --> 00:24:04.020
Well done on this task. You've done brilliantly.

636
00:24:04.020 --> 00:24:04.980
The Indonesian government

637
00:24:04.980 --> 00:24:07.410
is successfully managing inequality in Jakarta.

638
00:24:07.410 --> 00:24:09.030
I would like you to place a cross on the line

639
00:24:09.030 --> 00:24:11.640
representing your opinion, whether you agree or disagree,

640
00:24:11.640 --> 00:24:13.170
and then justify your opinion.

641
00:24:13.170 --> 00:24:14.550
Use information from this lesson

642
00:24:14.550 --> 00:24:16.920
and your own research to support your answer.

643
00:24:16.920 --> 00:24:18.390
Pause the video here whilst you decide,

644
00:24:18.390 --> 00:24:20.603
and press play when you're ready to continue.

645
00:24:25.380 --> 00:24:27.780
Excellent. Let's check our answers.

646
00:24:27.780 --> 00:24:29.850
Your response could look something like this.

647
00:24:29.850 --> 00:24:32.850
I have placed it closer to the disagree side.

648
00:24:32.850 --> 00:24:35.100
Your response may look something like this:

649
00:24:35.100 --> 00:24:36.600
I disagree with the statement.

650
00:24:36.600 --> 00:24:38.220
While the government has introduced reforms

651
00:24:38.220 --> 00:24:40.650
like flood defenses and proposed affordable housing,

652
00:24:40.650 --> 00:24:42.330
the impact has been limited.

653
00:24:42.330 --> 00:24:43.800
The kampung upgrades have stalled,

654
00:24:43.800 --> 00:24:46.140
and transport link expansion is only promised,

655
00:24:46.140 --> 00:24:48.120
showing that not all plans are being delivered.

656
00:24:48.120 --> 00:24:50.010
The government is also spending 30 billion

657
00:24:50.010 --> 00:24:52.320
on building Nusantara, the new capital,

658
00:24:52.320 --> 00:24:54.240
while Jakarta still faces urgent needs

659
00:24:54.240 --> 00:24:57.060
like $6.5 billion of infrastructure upgrades

660
00:24:57.060 --> 00:25:00.120
and a shortage of 1.2 million affordable homes.

661
00:25:00.120 --> 00:25:02.250
Corruption and budget problems have slowed progress,

662
00:25:02.250 --> 00:25:05.670
and only 60% of kampung residents access education.

663
00:25:05.670 --> 00:25:07.110
These challenges show that inequality

664
00:25:07.110 --> 00:25:09.450
is not being effectively managed at present.

665
00:25:09.450 --> 00:25:10.620
Well done on this task.

666
00:25:10.620 --> 00:25:11.760
I hope you managed to include some

667
00:25:11.760 --> 00:25:13.850
of those points in your answer.

668
00:25:13.850 --> 00:25:15.060
We've now comes to the end of our learning

669
00:25:15.060 --> 00:25:16.770
on urban patterns in Jakarta,

670
00:25:16.770 --> 00:25:18.000
and you've done brilliantly.

671
00:25:18.000 --> 00:25:18.960
Before we end this lesson,

672
00:25:18.960 --> 00:25:21.000
let's summarize everything we've learned today.

673
00:25:21.000 --> 00:25:23.730
Rapid population growth has created significant inequalities

674
00:25:23.730 --> 00:25:25.740
in Jakarta's residential areas.

675
00:25:25.740 --> 00:25:27.660
People in poorer areas face overcrowding,

676
00:25:27.660 --> 00:25:29.490
flooding and poor sanitation.

677
00:25:29.490 --> 00:25:31.680
There are significant quality of life differences,

678
00:25:31.680 --> 00:25:34.830
with low-income areas often lacking basic services.

679
00:25:34.830 --> 00:25:37.140
Government reforms aim to reduce inequality,

680
00:25:37.140 --> 00:25:38.220
but many have stalled,

681
00:25:38.220 --> 00:25:40.830
and the move to a new capital city, Nusantara,

682
00:25:40.830 --> 00:25:43.530
is drawing funds away from Jakarta's urgent needs.

683
00:25:43.530 --> 00:25:45.450
Well done in this lesson, you've done brilliantly,

684
00:25:45.450 --> 00:25:47.873
and I look forward to learning with you again very soon.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Rapid population growth creates opportunities for people in Jakarta.
Rapid population growth has provided opportunities to access resources in Jakarta.
Rapid population growth has provided employment opportunities in Jakarta.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Both sectors also create job opportunities. Schools, hospitals, and research centres employ many people, and better education leads to higher-skilled, better-paid work.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Education and healthcare in Jakarta only improve wellbeing, not economic opportunities.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain how population growth has created opportunities for people in Jakarta.

lessons.transcript_sentences:
Hello and welcome.
My name is Ms. Harrison and I'm so excited to be learning with you today.
Today's lesson is called Opportunities for People Living in the City.
Grab everything you might need for today's lesson and let's begin our learning.
By the end of today's lesson, you'll be able to explain how population growth has created opportunities for people in Jakarta.
Before we can begin this learning, we need to find the keywords that we'll be using throughout today's lesson.
The keywords are access, opportunity, and employment.
Access, this the ability people have to make use of essential services such as water, electricity, healthcare, and education.
Opportunity, this is a positive feature or benefit that improves people's lives, such as access to clean water, jobs, healthcare or education.
Employment, this the availability of jobs and work for people, often used to measure economic opportunity and development.
Now that we've defined these keywords, we can begin our learning.
The first question we are going to explore in today's lesson is how has access to resources improving in Jakarta? Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia and it's one of the fastest growing cities in the world.
It's home to over 10 million people and that number keeps rising.
As more and more people move to the city, either from rural areas or from overseas, the pressure on services is increasing.
Because of this rapid population growth, Jakarta's government and planners have to constantly adapt and upgrade the city's services.
Today, we are going to look at how urbanization is shaping life in Jakarta through its opportunities.
What might a growing city need more of? Pause the video here whilst do you have a think and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
A growing city might need more of water, energy, jobs, education, and healthcare.
Well-done if you managed to come up with some of those as well.
Investment is increasing access to safe and clean water.
This timeline shows how Jakarta improving access to clean water, and it also highlights a key opportunity that comes with urban growth.
In 2010, most people were reliant on groundwater and that's not ideal in a crowded city, it can lead to pollution and even land subsidence, but urban growth can attract investment like what we see in 2015, when the city began improving its piped water systems, by 2020, half of the city had access to clean water, and that's just not a statistic.
It's an opportunity for better quality of life.
With safer water, there's less disease, better hygiene and improved health, especially in low income areas.
As access rises to 65% in 2024 and eventually 100% by 2030, the opportunities continue to grow, better water services mean more people can spend less time collecting water.
Children are more likely to attend school and the city becomes more attractive for businesses and tourism.
So while rapid urbanization can bring about challenges, it also creates opportunities for development, infrastructure, and improving lives and Jakarta's access to water is a perfect example of that.
How does access to clean water create opportunities for people? Pause video here whilst you have a think and press play when you're ready to continue.
Fantastic.
Let's hear some answers.
Aisha said, "Access to clean water improves health by reducing the spread of disease.
When people are healthier, they can attend work or school, which increases opportunities." And Alex said, "Reliable water supply support small businesses like food vendors, which depend on clean water.
This helps to create jobs and boost the local economy, especially in poorer areas." I hope you managed to come up with some of those ideas as well.
True or false? By 2024, over 90% of Jakarta's residents had access to safe and clean water.
Pauses video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Fantastic.
This statement was false.
I would like you to explain why.
Pause video here and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The reason why this statement is false is because in 2024, only 65 residents had access to water.

lessons.lessonTitle: Effects of population growth on spatial growth, functions and land use
lessons.unitTitle: Jakarta: case study of a major city in an emerging country

lessonKeywords.description: a city with a population of over 10 million people
open land with vegetation, such as parks, gardens, forests or wetlands
informal settlements in Indonesia. Homes are self-built, crowded together and may lack access to sanitation and electricity

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Population growth has affected the pattern of spatial growth in Jakarta.
Population growth has affected changing urban functions in Jakarta.
Population growth has affected land use in Jakarta.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Different parts of Jakarta are changing in different ways. West Jakarta is losing green space to malls and housing, East Jakarta is growing with factories and roads, South Jakarta has gated communities, and Central Jakarta is focused on business.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: All areas of Jakarta are experiencing the same kind of land use change and impacts.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe how population growth has affected the pattern of spatial growth and changing urban functions and land use in Jakarta.

teacherTips.teacherTip: GIS can help students see how Jakarta’s land use changed from 2000 to 2020. They can use maps to spot green space loss, urban sprawl, and link it to data like population or flood risk.

lessons.unitTitle: Jakarta: case study of a major city in an emerging country

lessonKeywords.description: the purpose or function of land, for example: residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural or recreational use
the CBD is the commercial and business centre of a city, usually with high land values, tall buildings and a concentration of shops, offices and services
the area at the edge of a city where urban land uses (like housing or industry) meet rural land uses (like farmland or open space)

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Jakarta exhibits characteristic urban forms (CBD, inner city, suburbs and rural-urban fringe).
Jakarta's structure (urban form) is determined by function and buildling age.
Jakarta is rapidly expanding into surrounding rural areas, changing land use dramatically.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Jakarta’s suburbs include both wealthy and mid-income areas, many of which are well-planned and developed (e.g. Pondok Indah, Kelapa Gading).
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Jakarta’s suburbs are poor and unplanned with informal settlements.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain factors influencing Jakarta's urban structure.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Use Google Earth or GIS platforms such as ArcGIS to explore land use in Jakarta’s suburbs and rural-urban fringe.

lessons.lessonTitle: Challenges caused by rapid urban population growth: housing
lessons.unitTitle: Jakarta: case study of a major city in an emerging country

lessonKeywords.description: an informal settlement in Indonesian cities that is self-built without planning permission. Homes are overcrowded, poorly constructed, and lack basic services
the basic services and facilities needed for a city to function, such as water supply, electricity, sewage systems, transport and waste collection
a waterborne disease caused by bacteria in contaminated water or food. It spreads quickly in areas with poor sanitation and can cause severe diarrhoea and dehydration

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: There are challenges for people living in Jakarta.
Rapid population growth has created housing shortages in Jakarta.
Rapid population growth has led to the development of squatter and slum settlements in Jakarta.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Not all people in Jakarta have equal access to safe housing with running water. Poorer communities, especially in informal settlements, often lack basic services, while wealthier areas have more reliable infrastructure.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: All people in Jakarta have equal access to safe housing with running water.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain how rapid population growth in Jakarta has led to housing issues.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Students could use Street View to compare housing types and quality in different areas of Jakarta.

00:20:56.010 --> 00:20:58.440

00:21:18.270 --> 00:21:19.500
where there's a high risk of flooding,

Fires like this spread quickly

due to flammable materials used in construction

and lack of access for emergency services.

569
00:21:34.080 --> 00:21:36.750
Kampung homes are often made from scrap wood, metal sheets

570
00:21:36.750 --> 00:21:40.290
and plastic, most lack basic access to safe electricity,

571
00:21:40.290 --> 00:21:41.910
and in some cases, power is shared

572
00:21:41.910 --> 00:21:44.520
or tapped illegally, increasing the risk of blackouts

581

You've done brilliantly and I look forward to learning

lessons.lessonTitle: Location and national, regional and global context of Jakarta
lessons.unitTitle: Jakarta: case study of a major city in an emerging country

lessonKeywords.description: a city with a population of over 10 million people
the sinking or settling of land, often caused by human activities such as excessive groundwater extraction, which can increase the risk of flooding
a city with global influence, important in the world economy through finance, trade, culture and communication

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Jakarta is a global megacity located on the island of Java and is the capital of Indonesia.
Jakarta has distinctive characteristics of site, situation and connectivity.
Jakarta is important nationally, regionally and internationally.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Jakarta is not just important because it’s the capital. It also plays a major role nationally as Indonesia’s economic centre and globally through its trade, transport links, and role as the ASEAN headquarters.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Jakarta is only important nationally because it is the capital city.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe the location and context of Jakarta.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Use GIS to map Jakarta’s transport links and flood risk areas, helping students understand its national and global connectivity, as well as why environmental challenges like subsidence and flooding are driving the capital’s relocation.

lessons.unitTitle: Jakarta: case study of a major city in an emerging country

lessonKeywords.description: small-scale projects led by local people to meet community needs, often supported by NGOs
development that meets the needs of people today without damaging the environment or reducing resources for future generations
a group of people working together to achieve shared goals. A housing cooperative is where residents help plan and manage their homes, often in partnership with local government or NGOs

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Bottom-up strategies involving community and NGO-led can make Jakarta more sustainable.
Bottom-up housing projects have been successful in improving housing.
Bottom-up housing projects have been successful in improving health and education.
There are advantages and disadvantages of 'bottom-up' strategies for improving health and education services.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Bottom-up strategies are valuable because they reflect community needs, improve trust, and lead to long-term change. However, they usually require support from NGOs or the government, such as funding, land rights, or technical help to be sustainable.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Bottom-up strategies can fully solve urban problems on their own.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain advantages and disadvantages of bottom-up strategies for achieving sustainability in Jakarta.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Students could make use of ArcGIS’s Wayback feature to explore changes in Jakarta's residential areas.

lessons.unitTitle: Jakarta: case study of a major city in an emerging country

lessonKeywords.description: development led by governments or large organisations, often with large-scale funding and limited community input
services and facilities in a city, like transport systems, clean water supply, sewage networks and waste disposal, that help support people’s everyday needs
managing resources or services in a way that meets needs now without damaging the future

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: There are advantages and disadvantages of 'top-down' strategies for managing water supply.
There are advantages and disadvantages of 'top-down' strategies for managing waste disposal.
There are advantages and disadvantages of 'top-down' strategies for managing transport and air pollution in Jakarta.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Top-down strategies often improve infrastructure at a large scale, but they do not always reach all areas fairly. Wealthier areas tend to benefit first, while poorer communities may lack reliable water, waste collection, or transport access.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Top-down strategies always benefit everyone equally.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can assess the advantages and disadvantages of 'top-down' strategies for making Jakarta more sustainable.

lessons.transcript_sentences:
Hello and welcome.
My name is Ms. Harrison, and I'm so excited to be learning with you today.
Today's lesson is called Strategies for Achieving Sustainability: Top-down Strategies.
Grab everything you might need for today's lesson and let's begin our learning.
By the end of today's lesson, you'll be able to assess the advantages and disadvantages of top-down strategies for making Jakarta more sustainable.
Before we can begin this learning, we need to find the keywords that we'll be using throughout today's lesson.
The keywords are top-down development, infrastructure, and sustainable.
Top-down development, this is development led by governments or large organizations, often with large-scale funding and limited community input.
Infrastructure, these are services and facilities in a city like transport systems, clean water supply, sewage networks, and waste disposal that help support people's everyday needs.
Sustainable, this is managing resources or services in a way that meets needs now without damaging the future.
Now that we've defined these keywords, we can begin our learning.
The first question we're going to explore in today's lesson is, how has the government improved water supply? Top-down development is when governments or large organizations make decisions and lead major projects often on national or city-wide scale.
The key players in top-down development include governments, transnational corporations, and intergovernmental organizations like the World Bank or Asian Development Bank.
These players are involved in processes such as providing aid, giving loans, or investing through foreign direct investment.
The main aim of top-down development is to improve infrastructure, such as transport, water supply, electricity, and public services, often with the goal of boosting the economy and attracting investment.
Why might a government choose top-down over local-led development? Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
Let's hear some answers.
One student said, "Top-down development is faster, well-funded, and supports national goals, but it may ignore local people's needs.
Is that right?" Yes, that's correct.
Whilst top-down development is often faster and better funded because it's led by powerful organizations like governments and TNCs, which have access to large budgets, loans, and expertise, these projects usually support national goals, such as economic growth, improved infrastructure, or global investment.
However, a common criticism is that they ignore local needs because decisions are made by people at the top, often far from the communities affected.
Projects may fail to consider what local people actually want or need.
This can lead to solutions that are less effective, unsustainable, or even harmful for some groups, especially in poorer or informal areas.
So while top-down development can bring major benefits, it also risks leaving out the voices of those that's meant to help.
True or false.
Top-down development is always designed and led by local communities.
Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Fantastic.
This statement is false.
I would now like you to explain why.
Pause the video here and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The reason why the statement is false is because top-down development is led by governments or large corporations, not local communities.
It often aims to improve infrastructure at a citywide or national level.
Well done if you managed to explain that correctly.
You've done brilliantly.
By 2023, most of Jakarta's water system was privately managed and many people lacked safe drinking water.
Laura has said, "Not everyone had access to water and some of the water people have access to was contaminated with chemicals and toxins, which could make people ill with cholera.
Is that right?" Yes, she's correct.
And Sofia said, "Some kampungs did not have access to water and people had to use wells or spend money on bottled water".
And that's also correct.
And spending money on bottled water was an extreme financial burden for those people.
What would a more sustainable water supply look like? Jakarta's current water supply is not sustainable.
Too many people rely on groundwater and this is causing the land to sink, a process known as subsidence.
If more people had access to piped, treated water, the need to extract ground water would fall, helping to protect the land and make the city more sustainable.
Another solution is rainwater harvesting, collecting and storing rainwater for household use.
This would help to reduce the demand on ground water.
Jakarta's rivers are heavily polluted with sewage and industrial waste, making them unsafe and unusable.
Right now, this is not a sustainable water system.
If waste water treatment improved, less sewage would enter the rivers, and if forests and wetlands in the upstream areas were protected or restored, water quality would improve naturally.
Together, these changes would create a more sustainable and balanced water supply benefiting both people and the environment.
In recent years, Jakarta's government has taken major steps to improve access to clean and reliable water.
Back in 2010, much of the city still relied on groundwater, which was leading to problems that land subsidence and unsafe drinking water.
By 2015, the government began investing in piped water systems to reduce dependence on wells.
Progress was slow at first.
By 2020, only 50% of residents had access to piped water.
By 2023, the city ended private ownership of water services.
Control was handed over to PAM Jaya, a public provider to make water access more fair and affordable.
By 2024, coverage had improved 65% of residents, a clear sign of progress.
The city's goal is to reach 100% access by 2030, ensuring that everyone in Jakarta's safe, treated water in their homes.
Are Jakarta's water services becoming more sustainable? Pause the video here whilst you have a think and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
So yes, Jakarta's water service is becoming more sustainable, but there is still progress to be made.
The city has taken important steps like reducing reliance on groundwater, which has been causing land subsidence.
Investments in piped water systems mean more people now have access to clean, treated water.
In 2023, the government returned water services to public control, aiming to make access more affordable and reliable.
By 2024, 65% of residents had piped water with the goal of reaching 100% by 2030, a move that supports long-term sustainability.
However, challenges remain.
Water pollution, limited waste water treatment, and unequal access and poorer areas still pose risks.
So while Jakarta is clearly moving in the right direction, continued investment and better management are needed to make the system fully sustainable for everyone.
What change happened in Jakarta's water system in 2023? A, all residents gained access to clean water.
B, PAM Jaya took over from a private company.
C, the city began relying on more groundwater or D, a new landfill was open to manage waste.
Pause a video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The answer is B.
PAM Jaya took over from a private company.
Well done.
Top-down control of Jakarta's water service allows the government to invest in long-term infrastructure projects that improve access and protect the environment.
One major project is the water treatment plant.
Its purpose is to help fix leaks, upgrade old pipelines, and improve the overall efficiency of the water supply system.
The project also includes a goal to reforest river banks, which helps protect water quality by reducing pollution, erosion, and sediment flowing into rivers.
This is an example of how top-down investment can support sustainable water management, combining technology with the environmental protection to create a more reliable and cleaner water system for Jakarta's future.
Why would forests help make water supplying more sustainable? Pause the video here whilst you have a think and press play when you're ready to continue.
Fantastic.
Forests help make water supply more sustainable because they play a key role in protecting and improving water quality.
Trees and vegetation reduce soil erosion, which means less mud and sediment gets washed into rivers and reservoirs.
This keeps the water cleaner and reduces the need for expensive treatment.
Forests also filter pollutants and help to regulate water flow, reducing the risk of flooding during heavy rain and maintaining water levels during dry periods.
By restoring and protecting forested areas, Jakarta can improve the health of river systems, supporting biodiversity, and ensure a cleaner, more reliable water supply for the future.
I would like you to add the missing labels to the project, purpose and goal.
Pause the video here whilst you attempt this and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
These are the missing labels to the project, purpose and goal.
Well done if you manage to remember those.
Jakarta's government has made real progress in improving the city's water infrastructure, but there are still challenges around access and fairness.
On the one hand, top-down development has clear strengths.
The government has funded large-scale infrastructure with plans designed by experts, current systems now supply 4,750 liters of treated water every second.
However, local communities still have concerns.
Many feel their needs are not fully considered and that solutions may not be the right fit for their specific neighborhoods, especially in kampungs or poorer districts.
In many cases, low income areas receive improved services last, and when outside contractors are used, few local jobs are created.
Meaning residents may not see the full benefits.
So while the government-led projects can deliver widespread improvements, it's important to also include local voices to make sure development is fair and effective for everyone.
Which of the following reduces sustainability of Jakarta's top-down water strategy? Is it A, local needs are sometimes overlooked, B, access to pipe waters expanding, C, upstream areas are being reforested, or D, solutions might not fit certain neighborhoods? Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The answers are, A, local needs are sometimes overlooked, and D, solutions might not fit certain neighborhoods.
Well done if you identified those correctly.
I would now like you to fill in the blanks using the words below.
The text is discussing how has the government improved water supply.
Pause the video here whilst you attempt this task and press play when you're ready to continue.
Fantastic.
Let's check our answers.

In 2023, the government ended private control of water and handed it to PAM Jaya, a public provider.

We're now going to explore our second question of today's lesson.
How effective is Jakarta's waste strategy? Jakarta produces thousands of tons of waste every day, but until recently, there was no long-term sustainable system in place to manage it.
Much of the waste see the dumped in rivers, burned in open spaces or left in unofficial dumping sites where it causes serious pollution and health risks.
The city's main landfill, Bantar Gebang, is now overflowing with piles of rubbish reaching up to 50 meters high.

There are also very few recycling systems in place.
Most waste is mixed together with little sorting or reuse.
Meaning valuable materials are wasted and plastic pollution continues to build up.
Jakarta urgently needs a more sustainable waste management strategy to reduce environmental damage and protect public health.
Why is dumping waste like this not sustainable? Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Fantastic.
Dumping waste like this is not sustainable because it causes long-term damage to the environment, public health, and the economy.

lessons.transcript_sentences:
Hello and welcome.
My name's Ms. Harrison, and I'm so excited to be landing with you today.
Today's lesson is called "Trends and Causes of Population Growth in Jakarta".
Grab everything you might need for today's lesson and let's begin our learning.
By the end of today's lesson, you'll be able to explain factors that have contributed to Jakarta's population growth.
Before we can begin this learning, we need to define the keywords that we'll be using throughout today's lesson.
The keywords in today's lesson are: mega city, migration, and natural increase.
Mega city: This is a city with a population of over 10 million people.
Migration: This is the movement of people from one place to another, either within a country or between countries, often for economic, social, political, or environmental reasons.
Natural increase: This is the difference between the birth rate and death rate of a population.
This occurs when the birth rate is higher than the death rate.
Now that we've defined these keywords, we can begin our learning.
The first question we're going to explore in today's lesson is, how has Jakarta's population changed? In 1950, Jakarta had a population of over one million people.
Since then, the city has grown rapidly.
Today, it is a bustling mega city with a population of over 11.
6 million in the city itself, and over 30 million in the wider metropolitan area.
This dramatic growth has transformed Jakarta from a small urban center into one of the largest and most important cities in Southeast Asia.
What factors do you think drive these changes? Pause the video here whilst you have a think, and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
Some of the factors that have driven these changes are: healthcare, education, urbanization, jobs, and laws.
Well done if you identified those as well.
Jakarta's population has climbed steadily since the mid-20th century, especially after Indonesia's independence in 1945.
In 1950, the population grew to around 1.
4 million, and by the 1970s it had grown to over six million.
And by 2004, Jakarta officially became a mega city with a population surpassing 10 million.
Much of this growth has been driven by rapid rural-to-urban migration as people move to the city in search for work, education, and better services.
Today, the population continues to rise, and by 2025 it is expected to reach over 11.
6 million within the city limits, with far more in the greater Jakarta area.
Which of these made the biggest change in Jakarta's population growth? Was it A, rural-to-urban migration? B, independence in 1945? C, COVID-19? Or D, suburbanization? Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The answer is A, rural-to-urban migration.
Well done if you identified that correctly.
When did Jakarta become a mega city? A, in 1945? B, 1996? C, 2001? Or D, 2004? Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The answer is D, 2004.
Well done if you identified that correctly.
Population pyramids help us understand patterns in birth rates, death rates, life expectancy, and population growth.
They can also show how population's changing over time, whether it's young and growing or aging and declining.
What's different or similar between 1960 and 2024 for Jakarta's population pyramid? Pause the video here whilst you take a closer look at them and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
Let's take a closer look.
These two population pyramids show Jakarta's population structure has changed between 1960 and 2024.
We're going to focus on the similarities.
In both years, there are more people aged zero to 59 than people aged 60 and over.
This shows that Jakarta still has a relatively young population.
We can also see that there are more older females aged 60-plus than older males, and this reflects a longer life expectancy for women.
Now let's look at the differences.
There are clear differences between Jakarta's population in 1960 and 2024.
In 2024, we can see there are more working-age adults between 20 and 59 compared to 1960.
This shows that Jakarta now has a much larger and more active workforce supporting economic growth.
The number of children being born has decreased, shown by the narrower base of the pyramid in 2024.
This reflects a decline in birth rates over time.
There is also a noticeable increase in the number of older people aged 60 and over in 2024.
This includes more old women than men due to higher female life expectancy.
Overall, the 2024 pyramid shows a more balanced but aging population compared to 1960's youthful, fast-growing population.
I would like you to identify which graph shows an aging population structure in Jakarta.
Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The answer is B.
Well done if you identified that correctly.
I would now like you to identify which graph shows a reduction in birth rates in Jakarta.
Pause the video here whilst you take a closer look and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The answer is B again.
Well done if you identified that.
I would now like you to describe the population change in Jakarta from 1950 to 2025, using the graph on your screen.
In your answer, I would like you to describe the trend, identify any anomalies, this is something that does not fit the trend that you've described, and use evidence to support your points.
Pause the video here whilst you attempt this task and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
Let's check our answers.
Your answer might include this, "Between 1950 and 2025, the population of Jakarta increased significantly.
In 1950, the population was around 1.
4 million.
It rose steadily through each decade, reaching 6.
5 million by 1980 and 8.
2 million by 1990.
By 2004 the population hit 10 million, meaning Jakarta became a mega city.
Although growth slowed slightly between 2004 and 2015, the overall trend has been upward.
By 2025, the population is projected to reach 11.
6 million.
This shows continuous growth over 75 years." Well done if you managed to include some of those points in your answer.
We're now going to explore our second question of today's lesson: How does migration add to Jakarta's population? Jakarta's population has grown over time due to two main factors, natural increase and migration.
Natural increase happens when the number of births is higher than the number of deaths.
Jakarta has a youthful population with a large share of young adults.
This age group is most likely to have children, which has contributed to population growth in the past.
However, natural increase now plays a smaller role in Jakarta's growth.
The birth rate, the number of births per 1,000 people per year, is falling, as families choose to have fewer children and access to education and healthcare improves.
As a result, migration has become the main driver of Jakarta's population growth today.
The graph on your screen is showing birth rates versus death rates in Jakarta from 1960 to 2025.
And as we can see, there's a clear decline.
What do you think is causing birth rates and death rates to fall in Jakarta? Pause the video here whilst you have a think and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
Andeep says, "Is it linked to better access to healthcare and jobs? This means life expectancy is increasing, right?" Andeep is correct.
Birth rates in Jakarta are falling, and there are several reasons why.
As access to education improves, especially for women, people are choosing to delay starting having families.
More women are focusing on their careers, which often leads to having smaller family sizes.
There's also better access to contraception, giving people more control over when and how many children they have.
And in crowded, expensive cities like Jakarta, the cost of raising children is high, so many families choose to have fewer children.
At the same time, death rates are falling too.
This is because of better healthcare with more hospitals, vaccinations, and access to medicine.
People also benefit from cleaner water, improved sanitation, and higher living standards, all of which help people live longer and healthier lives.
These changes are signs of Jakarta's growing level of development and urbanization.
What does natural increase mean? Is it A, the total number of people immigrating into a country? B, the difference between the number of births and the number of deaths in a population? C, the overall growth of a population including migration? Or D, the rate at which the economy of a country grows naturally? Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The answer is B, the difference between the number of births and the number of deaths in a population.
Well done if you identified that correctly.
Based on the graph, what is the approximate percentage decrease in the birth rate from 1960 to 2025? When we're looking at percentage decreases, this is how we work it out: We subtract the new value from the original value and divide that by the original value and times by 100.
Pause the video here whilst you attempt this task and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The answer is C, 59.
Well done on this.
Many Indonesians are leaving their rural villages to move to Jakarta in search for better lives.
This is known as rural-to-urban migration.
There are several push factors that drive people away from the countryside.
These include crop failure, which affects farming families, a lack of job opportunities, and poor access to education and healthcare in rural areas.
At the same time, Jakarta offers a range of pull factors that attract people to the city.
These include more jobs, better schools and hospitals, and the appeal of a more modern lifestyle.
Together, these push and pull factors help explain why so many people moved to Jakarta, adding to the city's rapid population growth.
Many people move from rural areas like Papua to urban centers like Jakarta because of the clear differences in opportunities and living conditions.
In Jakarta, people can earn higher wages, with a GDP per capita of around $14,000 US.
The city offers jobs in industry, technology, and finance, along with good infrastructure, clean water, and better access to education and healthcare.
In contrast, Papua has a much lower GDP per capita, around $3,000 US.
Most people work in farming and mining and wages are lower.
The region also struggles with poor roads, limited access to clean water, and fewer healthcare and education services.
These differences act as strong push and pull factors, encouraging people to migrate from rural areas to cities in search of a better quality of life.
True or false: Access to education and healthcare can be both a push and a pull factor depending on the location.
Pause the video here whilst you decide and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
This statement is true.
I would now like you to explain why.
Pause the video here and press play when you're ready to continue.
Excellent.
The reason why the statement is true is because in rural areas, poor or limited access to schools and medical services can push people to leave.
In contrast, cities like Jakarta often offer better education and healthcare, which pull people in.
It is important, therefore, to say what kind of access to education or healthcare you're talking about, good or bad.
Well done if you managed to explain that correctly, you've done brilliantly.

Jakarta's growing economy brings opportunities,

has brought many opportunities,

As the city expands,

education, and healthcare,

while many low-income families,

00:19:28.620 --> 00:19:29.640
As the population grows,

hospitals, transport, and housing,

00:19:36.120 --> 00:19:38.070

limited job security, and end up in squatter settlements.

you've done brilliantly.

I would now like you to describe

and they help to improve infrastructure.

And Alex said, "Jakarta's population has increased over time

00:20:53.130 --> 00:20:55.343
and press play when you're ready to continue.

"Economic growth in Jakarta has caused population change

because it attracts investment

from both Indonesian and international companies.

invest money to build offices,

factories, and infrastructure.

This investment creates jobs

for both skilled and unskilled workers.

00:21:26.970 --> 00:21:27.840

00:21:27.840 --> 00:21:28.890
I hope you managed to include

00:21:28.890 --> 00:21:31.110
some of those points in your answer.

00:21:31.110 --> 00:21:32.700
We've now come to the end of our learning

541
00:21:32.700 --> 00:21:35.040
on "Trends and Causes of Population Growth in Jakarta",

542
00:21:35.040 --> 00:21:36.390
and you've done brilliantly.

543
00:21:36.390 --> 00:21:37.380
Before we end this lesson,

544
00:21:37.380 --> 00:21:39.690
let's summarize everything we've learned today.

545
00:21:39.690 --> 00:21:42.240
Jakarta's grown into one of the world's largest cities,

546
00:21:42.240 --> 00:21:45.240
with a population of 11.6 million in the city itself

547
00:21:45.240 --> 00:21:48.060
and over 30 million in the greater Jakarta area.

548
00:21:48.060 --> 00:21:50.580
This rapid growth has been driven by three main factors:

549
00:21:50.580 --> 00:21:53.250
natural increase, migration, and economic growth.

550
00:21:53.250 --> 00:21:55.200
The first factor is natural increase,

551
00:21:55.200 --> 00:21:56.520
and this happens when there are more births

552
00:21:56.520 --> 00:21:58.140
than deaths in a population.

553
00:21:58.140 --> 00:21:59.640
Jakarta has a youthful population,

554
00:21:59.640 --> 00:22:00.840
meaning a large share of people

555
00:22:00.840 --> 00:22:03.420
are in the age group most likely to have children.

556
00:22:03.420 --> 00:22:06.090
As a result, the population has grown steadily.

557
00:22:06.090 --> 00:22:07.200
However, it's important to know

558
00:22:07.200 --> 00:22:09.060
that birth rates are now falling

559
00:22:09.060 --> 00:22:10.530
as families choose to have fewer children

560
00:22:10.530 --> 00:22:13.080
and access to education and healthcare improves.

561
00:22:13.080 --> 00:22:15.240
The second major factor is migration.

562
00:22:15.240 --> 00:22:17.580
Many people move from rural areas of Indonesia,

563
00:22:17.580 --> 00:22:20.460
such as Papua and Sulawesi, in search of better jobs,

564
00:22:20.460 --> 00:22:22.080
education, and healthcare.

565
00:22:22.080 --> 00:22:24.270
This is known as rural-to-urban migration.

566
00:22:24.270 --> 00:22:26.190
In addition, international migration

567
00:22:26.190 --> 00:22:27.720
also contributes to growth.

568
00:22:27.720 --> 00:22:29.700
Skilled workers and professionals from countries like

569
00:22:29.700 --> 00:22:32.280
China, South Korea, Japan, and the USA

570
00:22:32.280 --> 00:22:34.470
come to Jakarta for business opportunities,

571
00:22:34.470 --> 00:22:35.760
especially in growing industries

572
00:22:35.760 --> 00:22:37.740
like technology and finance.

573
00:22:37.740 --> 00:22:39.660
The third factor is economic growth.

574
00:22:39.660 --> 00:22:41.700
Jakarta is the economic center of Indonesia

575
00:22:41.700 --> 00:22:44.250
and a key player in the Southeast Asian region.

576
00:22:44.250 --> 00:22:45.840
Many transnational corporations

577
00:22:45.840 --> 00:22:49.530
such as Samsung, Shell, and HSBC have invested in the city.

578
00:22:49.530 --> 00:22:52.080
Their presence creates jobs, builds infrastructure,

579
00:22:52.080 --> 00:22:54.450
and attracts even more workers and businesses.

580
00:22:54.450 --> 00:22:56.190
This leads to the multiplier effect,

581
00:22:56.190 --> 00:22:59.250
where economic activity keeps generating further growth.

582
00:22:59.250 --> 00:23:00.960
Together, these three forces,

583
00:23:00.960 --> 00:23:03.000
natural increase, migration, and investment,

584
00:23:03.000 --> 00:23:05.490
have helped transform Jakarta into a mega city

585
00:23:05.490 --> 00:23:08.460
with both great opportunities and major challenges.

586
00:23:08.460 --> 00:23:10.287
Well done on today's lesson, you've done brilliantly.

587
00:23:10.287 --> 00:23:13.087
And I look forward to learning with you again very soon.

lessonKeywords.description: the decline and loss of traditional forms of industry
labour-intensive industries such as coal mining, steel and textile production and ship building
an increased connectedness between different countries that spreads money, ideas, goods and people
the takeover of state-run industries by private corporations

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: There have been major changes in the economy of the UK.
De-industrialisation and the decline of traditional industrial base have caused economic change in the UK.
Globalisation has caused economic change in the UK.
Government policies have caused economic change in the UK.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Some areas, such as the north east, continued to rely on traditional industries until the 1980s and 1990s. Other areas, like London, moved into tertiary industries long before others.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: The changes in the UK economy affected all regions equally and at the same time.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe the main causes of economic change in the UK.

teacherTips.teacherTip: It can be difficult for students to understand what life was like in areas dominated by traditional industries. Using short clips from films can help them to see the dependence families had on particular industries.

lessons.lessonTitle: Social and economic changes in the rural landscape

lessonKeywords.description: the movement of people to rural areas from urban ones
the growth of the population through its rise in birth rate and/or decline in death rate
green space around cities for which there are strict planning controls to preserve natural spaces and prevent urban sprawl
someone who lives a distance from where they work and has to regularly travel between the two locations

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: The rural landscape in the UK has experienced social and economic change.
The rural landscape in South Cambridgeshire has experienced social and economic changes due to population growth.
The rural landscape in Gwynedd has experienced social and economic changes due to population decline.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: While retirees moving into a rural area may be able to live comfortably, local people may experience a stagnation in employment opportunities and not be able to afford to live where they grew up.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Everyone living in a rural area will have a higher standard of living.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can assess the impacts of rural population growth and decline.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Discussing population growth and decline provides opportunities for students to practise calculating percentage increase and decrease from raw data.

lessons.lessonTitle: Improvements and new developments in transport

lessonKeywords.description: money given to someone as recognition of the loss of something (such as their land) when there is a need to build on it
something that crosses the Atlantic Ocean
a network that keep homes and businesses functioning such as roads, rail lines, pipelines and energy grids

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: There have been improvements in the UK's transport infrastructure.
There have been improvements in road and rail infrastructure in the UK.
There have been improvements in port and airport capacity in the UK.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: In most cases the jobs created by building infrastructure projects are likely to be short term and highly specialist. This means they are unlikely to last the length of the build time.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Building infrastructure projects will create long term employment opportunities.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can analyse the impacts and potential impacts of new developments in transport infrastructure.

teacherTips.teacherTip: It is hard to imagine the scale of Liverpool2. Examine a satellite image of the site from which students can see individual containers and gain a better understanding of its size.

lessonKeywords.description: an economic phase where employment in manufacturing is replaced by employment in services and knowledge economies
a branch of industry that manages money and wealth, such as banking, insurance, fund management and taxation
money left over after someone has paid for their essentials such as food, bills and housing
an area of land dedicated to businesses specialising in science and technology

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: The UK is moving towards a post-industrial economy.
The development of information technology has contributed to a post-industrial economy in the UK.
The growth of service industries, finance and research has contributed to a post-industrial economy in the UK.
Science and business parks have contributed to a post-industrial economy in the UK.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Research is an industry because it creates wealth through innovation and knowledge which has value.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Research is not a form of industry because it does not involve trade.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe the features of a post-industrial economy.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Look at maps, satellite images and street views of Cambridge Science Park to show students what the modern face of industry looks like.

lessons.lessonTitle: The place of the UK in the wider world

lessonKeywords.description: an international association of 56 countries that were previously part of the British Empire
the movement of people from one country to another
where two or more countries rely on each other

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: The UK has significant links with the wider world.
The UK has links to the wider world through trade, culture, transport and electronic communications.
The UK has economic and political links with the EU and the Commonwealth.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Commonwealth states meet every two years to promote trade relationships, human rights and development aid.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: The Commonwealth represents nothing more than a cultural and historical connection between countries.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can compare the UK's links with the wider world.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Students can make a list of their five favourites from different categories such as music artists, items of clothing, or foods and map where these things originate from to see how their lives link to other places.

Hello, my name is Chloe, and I'm a geography field studies tutor.

00:21:36.060 --> 00:21:40.050
that it was still in operation in relatively recent times.

482
00:21:40.050 --> 00:21:41.760
These countries are now independent,

483
00:21:41.760 --> 00:21:45.750
but they retain cultural and some political ties to the UK.

484
00:21:45.750 --> 00:21:47.340
Kenya is a great example.

485
00:21:47.340 --> 00:21:50.250
Although Swahili is one of the main languages spoken,

486
00:21:50.250 --> 00:21:53.253
English is also widely spoken throughout the country.

487
00:21:55.552 --> 00:21:58.080
So although of course the British Empire is no more,

488
00:21:58.080 --> 00:22:01.020
there is something called the Commonwealth Secretariat.

489
00:22:01.020 --> 00:22:03.270
It's an organization that helps member countries

490
00:22:03.270 --> 00:22:07.053
achieve sustainable development and economic prosperity.

491
00:22:07.890 --> 00:22:10.620
Member countries have shared common values

492
00:22:10.620 --> 00:22:15.180
and uphold and strive for free democratic rights.

493
00:22:15.180 --> 00:22:18.180
There's also something called preferential migration.

494
00:22:18.180 --> 00:22:20.580
This means that there's greater chance

495
00:22:20.580 --> 00:22:22.950
of moving between Commonwealth countries

496
00:22:22.950 --> 00:22:25.800
because you share that common history.

497
00:22:25.800 --> 00:22:27.780
You might have seen the monument

498
00:22:27.780 --> 00:22:29.400
which is in the photograph here.

499
00:22:29.400 --> 00:22:32.100
It's in Waterloo Station in London.

500
00:22:32.100 --> 00:22:34.230
It's the National Windrush Monument,

501
00:22:34.230 --> 00:22:36.570
and it pays tribute to the pioneering spirit

502
00:22:36.570 --> 00:22:41.370
of Caribbean migrants who came to the UK after World War II.

503
00:22:41.370 --> 00:22:43.500
And of course, many Caribbean countries

504
00:22:43.500 --> 00:22:45.240
were part of the Commonwealth,

505
00:22:45.240 --> 00:22:47.550
so that preferential migration link

506
00:22:47.550 --> 00:22:49.773
was really important at that point.

507
00:22:52.140 --> 00:22:53.010
There's also other ways

508
00:22:53.010 --> 00:22:55.320
that the member countries are linked together.

509
00:22:55.320 --> 00:22:56.760
There's preferential trade,

510
00:22:56.760 --> 00:22:59.760
and of course aid as well is more likely to flow

511
00:22:59.760 --> 00:23:02.583
between Commonwealth Secretariat members.

512
00:23:03.630 --> 00:23:06.240
There's also shared cultural and sporting events.

513
00:23:06.240 --> 00:23:08.580
The Commonwealth Games is a great example of this.

514
00:23:08.580 --> 00:23:09.900
It sees the Commonwealth countries

515
00:23:09.900 --> 00:23:12.363
compete against each other every four years.

516
00:23:14.970 --> 00:23:17.250
Let's check our understanding now. True or false?

517
00:23:17.250 --> 00:23:18.630
The Commonwealth of today

518
00:23:18.630 --> 00:23:21.600
is a cultural link between countries.

519
00:23:21.600 --> 00:23:23.373
Is that true or false?

520
00:23:28.740 --> 00:23:31.620
Well done if you recognized that is a false statement.

521
00:23:31.620 --> 00:23:33.153
Now tell me why it's false.

522
00:23:38.250 --> 00:23:40.650
So while cultural links do exist,

523
00:23:40.650 --> 00:23:43.500
the Commonwealth Secretariat aims to promote trade,

524
00:23:43.500 --> 00:23:46.950
democratic rights, and aid donations between members.

525
00:23:46.950 --> 00:23:51.063
It is not just a cultural link. It's far more than that now.

526
00:23:53.070 --> 00:23:55.050
Our final task of the day.

527
00:23:55.050 --> 00:23:57.780
Do you think it would be more beneficial for a country

528
00:23:57.780 --> 00:24:02.370
to be a member of the EU or the Commonwealth Secretariat?

529
00:24:02.370 --> 00:24:05.130
There's obviously advantages and disadvantages in both,

530
00:24:05.130 --> 00:24:07.740
so explain your reasons for your choice.

531
00:24:07.740 --> 00:24:10.140
This will take quite a bit of thought and time,

532
00:24:10.140 --> 00:24:11.670
so do pause the video now,

533
00:24:11.670 --> 00:24:14.243
and I'll come back to you with some ideas that I've got.

534
00:24:20.460 --> 00:24:23.670
Right, so your answer may include some of these ideas.

535
00:24:23.670 --> 00:24:25.410
I'm going to start off with the EU.

536
00:24:25.410 --> 00:24:27.330
So if you believe that the EU

537
00:24:27.330 --> 00:24:28.620
is going to be more beneficial,

538
00:24:28.620 --> 00:24:31.230
this is the kind of answer you might have given.

539
00:24:31.230 --> 00:24:32.820
I believe it would be more beneficial

540
00:24:32.820 --> 00:24:35.580
for a country to be a member of the EU.

541
00:24:35.580 --> 00:24:37.260
Though there are fewer member countries

542
00:24:37.260 --> 00:24:38.640
than in the Commonwealth,

543
00:24:38.640 --> 00:24:41.190
the trade agreement between the 27 members

544
00:24:41.190 --> 00:24:43.770
means a lot of goods can be traded freely,

545
00:24:43.770 --> 00:24:47.040
which benefits the economic growth of all countries.

546
00:24:47.040 --> 00:24:49.710
Remember that word, interdependence.

547
00:24:49.710 --> 00:24:52.560
Having the freedom to live and work across Europe

548
00:24:52.560 --> 00:24:54.270
means there is huge flexibility

549
00:24:54.270 --> 00:24:56.190
and greater choice of employment

550
00:24:56.190 --> 00:24:59.823
and the ability to fill skills gaps more easily.

551
00:25:00.840 --> 00:25:02.160
Now let's look at the other side of things.

552
00:25:02.160 --> 00:25:05.010
Some of you might have chosen the Commonwealth Secretariat

553
00:25:05.010 --> 00:25:08.133
as the organization that you'd rather be a member of.

554
00:25:09.120 --> 00:25:09.953
Now you could have said,

555
00:25:09.953 --> 00:25:11.370
"I believe it would be more beneficial

556
00:25:11.370 --> 00:25:13.950
for a country to be a member of the Commonwealth.

557
00:25:13.950 --> 00:25:16.140
There are a lot more member countries in this alliance

558
00:25:16.140 --> 00:25:19.080
and they are spread out over a greater amount of the world,

559
00:25:19.080 --> 00:25:21.930
making the membership more diverse, inclusive,

560
00:25:21.930 --> 00:25:25.260
and therefore possibly more outward-looking.

561
00:25:25.260 --> 00:25:27.690
The common values that link the Commonwealth

562
00:25:27.690 --> 00:25:31.080
are important for countries socially and economically

563
00:25:31.080 --> 00:25:32.847
as well as politically."

564
00:25:35.340 --> 00:25:38.880
Let's now summarize our learning from today's lesson.

565
00:25:38.880 --> 00:25:40.770
The UK has economic, social,

566
00:25:40.770 --> 00:25:43.170
and political links to the wider world.

567
00:25:43.170 --> 00:25:46.050
Trade, transport links, electronic communication,

568
00:25:46.050 --> 00:25:47.490
and political alliances

569
00:25:47.490 --> 00:25:49.470
have been ways of increasing the number

570
00:25:49.470 --> 00:25:51.273
and the depth of connections.

571
00:25:52.260 --> 00:25:54.300
The UK's connection to the wider world

572
00:25:54.300 --> 00:25:56.790
have been felt through its cultural diversity,

573
00:25:56.790 --> 00:25:58.380
the changing political relationship

574
00:25:58.380 --> 00:26:00.000
it has with other countries,

575
00:26:00.000 --> 00:26:03.663
and the nature of the goods and media imports it receives.

576
00:26:05.310 --> 00:26:08.400
Well done. There was a lot of important learning there.

577
00:26:08.400 --> 00:26:11.040
I think it's really easy to get caught in the idea

578
00:26:11.040 --> 00:26:13.110
that the UK's links with other countries

579
00:26:13.110 --> 00:26:14.880
are kind of beyond us.

580
00:26:14.880 --> 00:26:17.880
They're political, they're to do with trade and economics,

581
00:26:17.880 --> 00:26:20.370
and it doesn't really affect our day-to-day lives.

582
00:26:20.370 --> 00:26:22.710
But of course, those things do affect us.

583
00:26:22.710 --> 00:26:24.180
The kind of people we are

584
00:26:24.180 --> 00:26:26.310
and the kind of people we interact with,

585
00:26:26.310 --> 00:26:29.610
the kind of goods we buy, the way we look, sound,

586
00:26:29.610 --> 00:26:30.840
and how we use media

587
00:26:30.840 --> 00:26:35.460
are all to do with our links with other countries.

588
00:26:35.460 --> 00:26:36.660
Have a look around you

589
00:26:36.660 --> 00:26:39.460
and see how well you're linked to the rest of the world.

lessons.lessonTitle: Impacts of industry on the physical environment

lessonKeywords.description: the pollution of air, water or land with something that is unnatural and harmful
being able to meet one's needs without compromising the ability to meet future needs
being able to produce the same level of output but through the use of less energy

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Industrial development can have negative impacts on the environment.
Newer industries can be more sustainable.
The Nissan plant in Sunderland illustrates how modern industrial development can be environmentally sustainable.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: All sectors of industry have the potential to harm the environment, though manufacturing continues to be highly wasteful.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Only manufacturing industries harm the environment.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe how industry can both negatively and positively affect the physical environment.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Hold a debate amongst students as to whether the manufacturing of electric cars is environmentally sustainable.

lessonKeywords.description: differences in the standard of living and wealth between two areas of the same country
the economic centre of a country or region; in the UK, this is London
the area of a country or region that serves the core and therefore has a weaker economy

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Regional differences exist in the UK between the north and the south.
Social and economic indicators can be used to identify a north-south divide in the UK.
There are strategies for resolving regional differences.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Though in general the north and south of the UK show evidence of economic inequality, there are lots of pockets of very high levels of wealth in the north and areas of extreme poverty in the south.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Everyone living in a particular region will have a similar lived experience of a place.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can evaluate strategies that attempt to resolve regional differences in the UK.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Students can look at current ONS data for areas in the north and south and evaluate if these have been successful in reducing regional inequality.

lessons.lessonTitle: Effects of climate change on people and the environment

lessonKeywords.description: when a weather event is significantly different from the average or usual weather pattern
the effect on people and communities due to an event or situation
a measure of the variety of living organisms within a particular habitat, ecosystem, biome, or all over Earth
when people lack secure access to sufficient amounts of safe and nutritious food for normal growth and development and an active and healthy life

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Climate change due to human activity is causing sea level rise, declining Arctic ice and more extreme weather events.
Climate change is affecting people and the environment.
With a range of projections, for example for global temperatures, there is uncertainty about future climates.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Different regions experience the effects of climate change differently due to environmental, economic and social factors.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: All regions will be equally affected by climate change.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain how climate change affects people and the environment.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Try to use up to date examples, news stories and where possible local/national effects to bring this concept to life, as well as more established examples and facts.
